class chapter V rising in the ranks The class that can fill any role, and changes shape to do it. Forever's changes are mostly about letting a druid stay in form. Night elf, High Order Skyborne Tauren, Windshaper Skyborne A druid can tank as a bear, deal damage as a cat or a spellcaster, and heal. Blizzard's summary is that druids "can perform any role" but give up some of the extras other classes bring: they cannot snare, silence or interrupt. Pick it if you can't decide what you want to be, or if you like the idea of being whatever the group is missing. Potions and most consumables work while shapeshifted, without dropping you out of form. Weapon enchantments and effects work in bear and cat form. Most doors and objects can be used without leaving form, and so can racial abilities. Revive, a new out-of-combat resurrection spell, is learned at level 12. Nature's Grasp and Omen of Clarity are learned by every druid rather than bought with talent points.

class chapter V rising in the ranks Damage from further away than anyone else, with an animal at your side. In Forever you can also choose to go without the animal. Dwarf, human, night elf, High Order Skyborne Orc, tauren, troll, Windshaper Skyborne Hunters have one job in a group, which is damage, and Blizzard says they have the longest range of any class. On your own, the pet takes the hits while you shoot. That makes the hunter the easiest class to play alone. The catch is the dead zone. Inside 8 yards a hunter's ranged attacks don't work, so the class is about keeping your distance. Aimed Shot is learned by every hunter at level 20. Traps can be used in combat. Pets grow stronger with the hunter's gear, and foxes are a new pet family. The talent trees allow a hunter with no pet at all, or one that moves between ranged and melee.

class chapter V rising in the ranks Frost and flame from a distance. Blizzard has not published its mage changes yet, so this page is short. Gnome, human, High Order Skyborne Orc, troll, undead Blizzard's description of the mage is a frail wizard who would rather not be hit, "hurling powerful bolts of frost and flame" from range. Mages also bring Polymorph, which takes one enemy out of a fight for a while. Blizzard has said that kind of crowd control still has a place in Forever's dungeons. Pick it if you like standing well back and seeing large numbers.

class chapter V rising in the ranks Plate armour and the Light. In Forever the paladin is on both factions for the first time. Human, dwarf Undead Blizzard wants paladins to work as tanks, healers or melee damage dealers, and has given each of those paths new tools. It has also kept the gaps: paladins still have no interrupt and no way to slow an enemy. Pick it if you want to be hard to kill and useful to everyone around you. On the Horde, that means playing an undead. Seals are no longer used up when you cast Judgment. Holy Strike, an instant weapon attack, is learned at level 6. Consecration is learned by every paladin at level 20. Seal of Fury is a new seal for tanking; while it is active, Judgment taunts.

class chapter V rising in the ranks Healing, protection and shadow damage. In Forever every priest gets tools that used to belong to one race. Dwarf, gnome, human, night elf Troll, undead Priests are the healers most groups look for first, and they can also turn to shadow magic and deal damage instead. Blizzard's changes keep that shape and widen who gets what. Each race of priest still has two spells of its own. Gnome priests, new in Forever, get Confounding Flash, which confuses up to five nearby enemies, and Contingency Plan, a ward that shields and heals a friend whose health drops low. Fear Ward and Devouring Plague are learned by every priest at level 20, whatever their race. Divine Spirit is learned by every priest at level 30. Shadow Word: Death is a new spell at level 32. Prayer of Healing heals the target's party rather than only the priest's own.

class chapter V rising in the ranks Stealth, poisons and picking your moment. Blizzard has not published its rogue changes yet, so this page is short. Dwarf, gnome, human, night elf, High Order Skyborne Orc, troll, undead, Windshaper Skyborne Blizzard describes rogues as relying on "a blend of stealth and minor mysticism", and adds that a rogue's allegiance "lasts only as long as the latest contract". Almost anyone can be one: every race in the game except the tauren. One change that applies to everybody helps here. Hit chance is now a single stat, and Blizzard says that makes tools such as poisons more reliable.

class chapter V rising in the ranks Totems and the elements. In Forever the shaman is on both factions for the first time. Dwarf Orc, tauren, troll, Windshaper Skyborne Blizzard's description is that shaman "use totems and spells to manipulate the elements" and push the fighters around them to greater strength. The 2004 guide called them the heart and soul of the Horde. They now belong to the Alliance as well, through the dwarves. That changes more than one class. Blizzard has already lowered the warrior's Battle Shout to allow for both factions having both shaman and paladin buffs.

class chapter V rising in the ranks Drains, fear and demons that do the work. Blizzard has not published its warlock changes yet, so this page is short. Gnome, human Orc, troll, undead Blizzard does not undersell this one. Its description begins "Warlocks are the bane of all life" and ends with "singular wickedness and cruelty". In practice a warlock wears an enemy down over time, takes health back from it and keeps a summoned demon at hand. Banish and Fear are among the crowd control tools Blizzard says still have a place in Forever's dungeons.

class chapter V rising in the ranks The armoured fighter at the front, and the one class every race on both factions can play. Dwarf, gnome, human, night elf, High Order Skyborne Orc, tauren, troll, undead, Windshaper Skyborne A warrior either tanks, holding the enemy's attention and taking the hits, or deals damage. Blizzard's summary is that any party or raid is happy to have one in either role, and that warriors lack the tools to recover easily from taking too much damage. They need a healer more than most. Everything a warrior does runs on Rage, which builds as you hit and get hit. Most of Forever's changes are about making that more dependable. Armor no longer reduces the Rage you gain from taking damage. Rage from dealing damage is based on weapon speed, with more from critical strikes. Victory Rush, learned at level 20, heals you for 10% of your health after a kill. Recklessness, Retaliation and Shield Wall no longer share a cooldown. A Protection talent lets you Charge while in Defensive Stance.

gear armor weapons equipment cloth leather mail plate shield wand stats what to wear What each of the nine classes wears and wields in Forever, what to look for on it, and what Blizzard has changed about gear. Short enough to read before you make a character. Gear does two jobs. Armor decides how hard you are to kill, and the numbers printed on it decide how well you do your job. Your class sets the limits: the heaviest armor you can put on and the kinds of weapon you can pick up. Inside those limits the choice is yours. Blizzard has said that itemization in Forever is changing to keep the gameplay of the original while "unsolving" the path through it. So the old best-in-slot lists are out of date, and the habits underneath them matter more than any single item. Spell, melee and ranged hit chance are one stat. So are the three kinds of critical chance. Weapon skill still works as before, but items carry less of it, "so they are not always the obvious best choice". Bonus healing also counts as one third as much bonus damage. Spellcaster weapons grant spell damage and healing. New stats: some items reduce the chance for your attacks to be parried or dodged. Some effects are tied to a kind of place (woodlands, mountains, deserts) or a kind of creature. Trinkets are being pushed toward situational effects. Unique dungeon boss items are blue quality, set bonuses are improved, and hundreds of new drops have been added. Quest rewards have been updated or added to so more classes and roles get something they can use. Transmog follows armor type: plate to plate, cloth to cloth. Weapon first For a warrior, rogue, paladin or hunter, a new weapon is the biggest single upgrade there is. In Forever that is true for casters as well: Blizzard says spellcaster weapons now grant spell damage and healing, so they "can look forward to level-up weapons in the same way Warriors, Rogues, and Hunters do". Then the heaviest armor you can wear You can always wear the lighter types too, and sometimes a lighter piece with the right stats wins. The 2004 guide's advice still reads well: basic armor matters most to the mail wearers, while cloth and leather classes get more from the stats on a piece than from its armor. Know your class's stats Every class has two or three numbers it wants more of. They are in the table above. An item without them is somebody else's item. Hit is one stat now, and so is crit Spell, melee and ranged hit chance are combined in Forever, as are the three kinds of critical chance. A piece with hit on it is good for any class that needs to land something. Green and near your level is enough The 2004 guide calls green items "par for a skilled adventurer" and says to keep them within three to five levels of your own. Don't spend your gold on gear while levelling. You will replace all of it. Run the dungeons Blizzard says every dungeon drop has been looked at again. Unique dungeon boss items are now blue quality, set bonuses have been improved, and quest rewards have been widened to cover more classes and roles. A one-handed weapon and a shield to tank, a two-hander to deal damage. The 2004 guide rates swords and axes a little above maces. The weapon, every time. Then the heaviest armor on offer, and a shield kept in your bags for dungeons. A one-hander and shield, or a two-hander. The guide's advice is that a weapon at your level matters more than which kind it is. A weapon that is current, a shield if you tank or heal, and enough intellect to keep casting. The bow or gun is the weapon that counts. Melee weapons are there for the stats on them. The ranged weapon first. Then agility on everything. A one-hander and a shield, or a two-hander for melee. The guide says shaman "require almost everything" from their stats. Decide whether you are healing, casting or hitting, and gear for that. Keep a shield either way. Daggers, swords, maces and fist weapons, one in each hand. In the 2004 guide, Backstab and Ambush need a dagger in the main hand. Two weapons that are current, and agility on the leather. Staves and maces. In Forever the weapon matters in animal form too. Pick the role first. A bear or cat now shops for weapons the way a warrior does. Maces, daggers and staves, and a wand for when the mana runs out. Healing gear does double duty now. Buy a wand early. A staff, or a dagger with an off-hand item. The guide's testers argued about which and called it a matter of style. For once, the weapon. Then intellect. A staff or a one-hander, and a wand. The 2004 guide says a good wand and high spirit and intellect are most of what a warlock needs. A caster weapon and a wand, then intellect.
faction alliance horde races choose side

Four old nations and one new arrival. In Forever the Alliance can field all nine classes for the first time, because dwarves can now be shaman. Blizzard describes the Alliance as "bound together by proud traditions of nobility, honor, faith, justice, and sacrifice". Three things are new on this side. Humans can be hunters, gnomes can be priests and dwarves can be shaman. The third matters most, because it gives the Alliance a class it has never had. The fifth race is new altogether. The High Order Skyborne are, in Blizzard's words, descendants of ancient scholars who have been called back to Azeroth to recover the knowledge they lost. The Skyborne exist on both factions, and you choose a side when you make one. Every race now has four racial traits, two you press and two that are always on. They are listed with each race above. Blizzard says several were reworked for Forever. Human Hunter, mage, paladin, priest, rogue, warlock, warrior Will to Survive, Perception, Sword Specialization, The Human Spirit Dwarf Hunter, paladin, priest, rogue, shaman, warrior Stoneform, Find Treasure, Mace Specialization, Big Game Hunter Gnome Mage, priest, rogue, warlock, warrior Escape Artist, Eureka!, Expansive Mind, Engineering Specialization Night Elf Druid, hunter, priest, rogue, warrior Elune's Light, Shadowmeld, Quickness, Wisp Spirit High Order Skyborne Druid, hunter, mage, rogue, warrior Walk on Air, Read Ley Line, Wind Blessed, Elemental Insight

Four old nations and one new arrival. In Forever the Horde can field all nine classes for the first time, because the undead can now be paladins. Blizzard describes the Horde as nations "loosely joined in an alliance of convenience against a hostile world that would see them destroyed". Three things are new on this side. Orcs can be mages, trolls can be warlocks and the undead can be paladins. The third matters most, because it gives the Horde a class it has never had. The fifth race is new altogether. The Windshaper Skyborne descend, in Blizzard's words, from the first of their people to receive the wind spirits' gift, and they have come to Azeroth to find out what happened to those spirits. The Skyborne exist on both factions, and you choose a side when you make one. Every race now has four racial traits, two you press and two that are always on. They are listed with each race above. Blizzard says several were reworked for Forever. Orc Hunter, mage, rogue, shaman, warlock, warrior Blood Fury, Shatter Curse, Axe Specialization, Hardiness Tauren Druid, hunter, shaman, warrior War Stomp, Cultivation, Plainsrunning, Endurance Troll Hunter, mage, priest, rogue, shaman, warlock, warrior Berserking, Rapid Regeneration, Beast Slaying, Regeneration Undead Mage, paladin, priest, rogue, warlock, warrior Will of the Forsaken, Cannibalize, Underwater Breathing, Touch of the Grave Windshaper Skyborne Druid, hunter, rogue, shaman, warrior Walk on Air, Skysight, Wind Blessed, Elemental Insight

skyborne shen'dorei new race high order windshaper zephras isle heroic pack The one race that is new in Forever. You can play a Skyborne on either faction, and the side you choose decides whether yours can be a mage or a shaman. The character creator has ten faces, nine skin colors from sky blue to peach to darker tones, three ear lengths, nine eye colors, feather colors, four face tattoos and two body tattoos, named Zephyr and Wayfinder. One body type has 21 hair styles and 13 facial hair options; the other has 25 hair styles and six styles of earring. Forever itself is included with a World of Warcraft subscription or game time. The Skyborne are an extra: Blizzard lists "Access to the new Skyborne race and their Zephras Isle starting experience" as the first item in the Skyborne Heroic Pack, and the Epic Pack contains everything in the Heroic Pack. The Heroic Pack also includes Early Name Reservation, which runs from October 27 to November 3. Blizzard also calls the Skyborne the shen'dorei, the hidden people. Thousands of years ago, in Blizzard's telling, a group of Highborne exiles made a pact with elemental wind spirits and built a civilization on Zephras Isle, inside Skywall, one of the elemental planes. That arrangement has broken down. The wind spirits have vanished, the pylons that hold the island together are failing, and Blizzard says the Skyborne are "divided over what comes next". The two playable versions are the two answers to that question. You choose a side when you make the character. Both versions start on Zephras Isle, which covers levels 1 to 12, and both can be druids, hunters, rogues and warriors. Blizzard says Skyborne druids get new forms made for the race. What the packs cost. We could not read a price on any Blizzard page; the shop asks for a login. Whether the Skyborne will ever be playable without a pack. How often Read Ley Line and Skysight can be used, and how long they last. Their mount, their home city and their languages. High Order Skyborne Descendants of the Highborne scholars of Eldre'Thalas. They decided that depending on the wind spirits had left their people vulnerable, and have returned to Azeroth "to reclaim the arcane knowledge that they have lost". Druid, hunter, mage, rogue, warrior Walk on Air Glide downward through the air for 10 seconds. Read Ley Line Activate a ley line to gain 100% increased health and mana regeneration. Wind Blessed 1% increased melee, ranged and spellcasting haste. Elemental Insight Damage to elementals increased by 5%. Windshaper Skyborne Descendants of the first shen'dorei to receive the wind spirits' gift. They have come to Azeroth "to solve the mystery of what became of their missing elemental mentors" and want the spirits restored. Druid, hunter, rogue, shaman, warrior Walk on Air Glide downward through the air for 10 seconds. Skysight Receive an Elemental Blessing increasing run speed by 10%. Wind Blessed 1% increased melee, ranged and spellcasting haste. Elemental Insight Damage to elementals increased by 5%.

elves elf night elf high elf blood elf sin'dorei quel'thalas sunwell highborne skyborne shen'dorei Four kinds of elf, one family tree. In World of Warcraft: Forever you can play a night elf or either version of the Skyborne. High elves and blood elves aren't playable. The short version: a night elf for the forest and the Alliance. A Skyborne for an elf on the Horde, or an elf mage on the Alliance. A blood elf only if you are happy to wait, and nobody knows for how long. Night elves came first. Blizzard says they founded a vast empire ten thousand years ago, and that their reckless use of magic brought it to ruin; in grief they withdrew to the forests. The 2004 guide adds that they vowed never to use magic again. In Forever they are Alliance and can be druids, hunters, priests, rogues or warriors. High elves are the ones who wouldn't give magic up. In the 2004 guide's history of Azeroth, a small band of night elves is exiled for keeping it, travels east and founds the kingdom of Quel'Thalas. Blizzard says the high elves of Quel'Thalas drew their strength from the Sunwell for thousands of years. They are not a playable race in Forever. Blood elves are high elves after the fall. Blizzard says an invasion by the undead Scourge decimated Quel'Thalas and cut its people off from the Sunwell, and the survivors took the name blood elves, or sin'dorei in their own tongue. In the modern game they are a Horde race. In Forever they are not playable, and no Blizzard post we have read says whether they ever will be. The Skyborne are the newcomers, and the only elves on both sides. Blizzard also calls them the shen'dorei: descendants of Highborne rebels who fled Eldre'Thalas and built a home in Skywall, one of the elemental planes, with the help of wind spirits. High Order Skyborne join the Alliance and can be mages. Windshaper Skyborne join the Horde and can be shaman. Both can be druids, hunters, rogues and warriors. The race comes with the Skyborne Heroic Pack, not the included game. Whether blood elves, high elves or Quel'Thalas will come to Forever later. A Blizzard forum thread paraphrases a September developer Q&A as a yes, but gives no quote, and no Blizzard post we can find says so.

Twenty-two episodes on twelve shows in the three weeks since BlizzCon. We went through every one: the show notes, the write-ups and the parts quoted on the record. Here's where they agree, where they argue, and what's missing from the conversation. Twenty-two episodes on twelve shows since BlizzCon. Most seem to agree Forever is slower and harder than people expected, and they argue about whether it's still Classic, whether you should pay for the new race, and whether playing the beta spoils launch. Almost nobody outside gaming is talking about it yet. Since Blizzard announced World of Warcraft: Forever at BlizzCon on September 12, we've found 22 podcast episodes about it on 12 different shows. Every one is linked on our podcasts page. Some are four-hour deep dives. Some give it twenty minutes between other news. Almost all of them are Warcraft shows or MMO shows. The only general gaming podcast we could confirm talking about it is the Giant Bombcast, about an hour and forty minutes into a show that was mostly about other things. We looked for episodes on the big tech, culture and business podcasts, from The Vergecast and Decoder to Hard Fork, NPR, Bloomberg and The Ringer, and found none. That's surprising. Blizzard is making Forever a permanent version of WoW, alongside the modern game and Classic, and Azeroth Morning Radio reports the beta crowds are big enough that Blizzard keeps adding capacity. For now, though, people who play WoW are the only ones talking about it. That may change on November 4. The most important show on the list belongs to Blizzard. World of Warcraft: Forever, the official podcast, started in September. Josh Corbett of Countdown To Classic hosts it, with Blizzard designers on every episode and a big streamer as guest: Xaryu in the first, Sodapoppin in the second. It's worth listening to. In the first episode Blizzard put its own beta data on the record for the first time: levels 1 to 20 are slower in Forever than in Classic Era, and some early blue quest rewards are being pulled back. The second is the designers explaining their class changes in their own words. Hosting it is a coup for Countdown To Classic, and it's easy to see why Blizzard asked: nobody independent has a bigger Classic audience. But it does mean the loudest independent voice on Forever now hosts the official show too, and his own show's latest episode reacts to an episode of the official one. That isn't a scandal, but it's worth knowing. Listen to both, and notice which one speaks more freely. This question runs through almost every episode. Azeroth United asks it outright: 'does WoW Forever still feel like Classic?' It's a fair question. The world and the level cap of 60 are the original ones, but Blizzard has added new zones, nine new dungeons, reworked talents, new race and class combinations, a new race, transmog and smaller raids. Blizzard's own answer, from game director Ion Hazzikostas in a BlizzCon interview with Warcraft Tavern, is that it's 'still the Classic assets, it's still the setting. But, boy, is the vibe just massively enhanced.' Lead classic designer Tim Jones put it more simply: 'The world is the main character.' If you want the before and after, Warcraft Brew spent the summer surveying fans on what Classic+ should be, then recorded their first beta impressions on September 21. Azeroth Morning Radio's 'What is Warcraft Forever?', recorded four days before the reveal, is a time capsule of what people expected. The surprise of the beta's first weeks is that most of the shows seem to welcome how slow it is. Blizzard's numbers say early levelling takes longer than in Classic Era, and the designers want gear to climb from white to green to blue at the old pace. Azeroth Morning Radio asks whether that slower, more dangerous open world will end up changing modern WoW as well. The classes are where it gets heated. Countdown To Classic spent a long stretch of 'The Dulltimate Warrior' arguing that the warrior still feels dull. When the designers explained their thinking on the official podcast, one forum thread called it the 'best interaction between fans and devs I have ever seen', while other players complained of a 'simple and stupid' design that removes 'fun, niche options'. The Blizzard Watch Podcast's 600th episode was recorded live while Liz Harper played the beta, and the crew split on it. Liz thinks playing early wears the shine off launch; Joe doesn't mind at all. It matters more than it sounds, because beta access is one of the things money buys. The Epic Pack includes it. The beta ends on October 21, and fan sites expect beta characters to be wiped, so for most players the first real character is the one they make on November 4. The Skyborne, Forever's new elf race, aren't part of the game your subscription gets you. They come in the paid Heroic Pack. Lore Watch, Blizzard Watch's lore show, goes at it from the story side and asks whether the Skyborne have enough history behind them to earn a place among the original races. Blizzard's line on the rest of the money question, from Clay Stone, is that there's no WoW Token and no paid boosts at launch, and no plans for them: 'You get better at the game by playing the game.' The beta's loudest news story this month has been about gold buying and a few big streamers. Countdown To Classic's 'Can't Buy Me Gold' covers it if you want it. We stay out of stories that are about people rather than the game, so it isn't part of this piece.

t: The guide says orcs can't be warriors
x: Every Horde race has warriors except the orcs, whose ranks were "depleted" by war. Orc warriors are playable, as they were on the first day of the original game. warrior Learning Your Place in the World In its overview of the classes, the 2004 guide goes through which races take up the warrior's trade. On the Alliance, all of them. On the Horde, tauren, trolls and undead. Then it adds that the orcs alone are left without, and gives a reason from the lore. It's the most confident mistake in the book. The guide went to print before the game was finished, and at some point between the writing and the launch the orcs got their warriors back. Orc warrior went on to be one of the best-known combinations in the game. This is why the book is worth reading now. It's a snapshot of a world that was still being decided.

t: Human hunters and five other firsts
x: Five races can be hunters: dwarf, night elf, orc, tauren and troll. Humans can be hunters too. It's one of six new race and class combinations. hunter Rising in the Ranks The hunter chapter opens with a table of starting attributes, one row for each race that can play the class. There are five rows. Human is not one of them. Blizzard has confirmed six new combinations for Forever: human hunter, gnome priest, dwarf shaman, orc mage, troll warlock and undead paladin. Some of them people have been asking about for two decades.

The goals of the undead "remain somewhat mysterious", and they are the only Horde race with no shaman. The undead can be paladins. paladin Learning Your Place in the World The 2004 guide didn't quite know what to make of the undead. In the class overview it sets them apart from the orcs, tauren and trolls, who share a set of beliefs, and leaves their aims as an open question. Forever gives them something nobody in 2004 would have guessed. Undead paladin is one of the six new combinations Blizzard has confirmed. The knights of Lordaeron, back for a second shift.

At level 40 you pay 80 gold for the mount and 20 for riding lessons. The fast mount at 60 costs 1,000. The cost moves into riding training, and learning to ride gives you a mount. No official price yet.  Joining the Troops The transport section lays it out plainly. Reach level 40, find 80 gold for the animal and another 20 for the lessons. For most players in 2004 that was more money than they had ever held, and the level 60 mount at 1,000 gold was a project for months. For Forever, Blizzard says the cost sits in the riding training and the mount comes with it. Blizzard has not announced a price or a level. Numbers are going around from people reading the beta's files, and we'll add them here when Blizzard confirms them.

t: Getting around: no flying, then or now
x: A hearthstone with a one hour cooldown, mage portals at level 40, and zeppelins that are free. No flying mounts. You cross the world on the ground.  Joining the Troops The 2004 guide's travel advice is a list of ways to avoid walking. The hearthstone takes you home once an hour, so it tells you to save it. Mages open portals to the cities from level 40. Zeppelins and boats cost nothing, which the book is plainly delighted about. Blizzard has confirmed that Forever has no flying mounts. Whether the hearthstone cooldown and the portal levels match the book is something Blizzard hasn't said, so for now those belong to 2004 only.

A happy pet does 125% damage. An unhappy one does 75% and starts to lose its loyalty. Blizzard hasn't said whether pet happiness returns. We're testing it in the beta. hunter Rising in the Ranks The hunter chapter gives pet happiness three levels: happy at 125% damage, content at 100% and unhappy at 75%. Let it stay unhappy and the pet thinks about leaving. There is a warning box about how much a pet eats. Blizzard's hunter post for Forever doesn't mention happiness at all. Rambleon is checking it in the beta, and this entry will be updated with what we find.

Your quiver takes a bag slot and your pet eats more than you do, so you have three bags for everything else. Blizzard hasn't said whether quivers and ammunition return. hunter Rising in the Ranks The guide is honest about the hunter's packing problem. One of your bag slots goes to the quiver or ammo pouch. A good share of what's left goes to pet food, because "you're feeding two after all." It then recommends skinning as a profession, which fills the remaining space with leather. Nobody has ever felt so seen by a book. Blizzard's posts about Forever don't say whether quivers and ammunition are back, so we make no claim either way.

Hunters are "almost as dangerous in melee" as at range. Leather armor until 40, then mail. Aimed Shot for every hunter at 20, traps usable in combat, pets that scale with your gear. The dead zone stays. hunter Rising in the Ranks The 2004 guide was optimistic about hunters up close. It describes them as nearly as dangerous in melee as they are with a bow, a view the next twenty years did not support. Blizzard's hunter post for Forever lists four changes. Aimed Shot comes to every hunter at level 20 instead of sitting in a talent tree. Traps can be used in combat. Your pet gets stronger as your gear does. And the dead zone stays: inside 8 yards, your ranged shots won't fire. Melee hunter remains a lifestyle choice.

A Horde town and an Alliance town with quests and monsters between them. You win by razing the other side's base. The new battleground is Darkspear Islands, 15 against 15.  To the Battle Nobody outside Blizzard had played a battleground when this chapter was written, so the guide describes the plan. Two towns, one for each faction. Quests and monsters in the land between. Victory when the enemy's base is razed "to the ground." The battlegrounds that shipped were tidier than that, though the description reads a lot like an early idea of Alterac Valley. Forever adds a new one, Darkspear Islands, for teams of 15.

t: Seventeen dungeons. That was the whole list.
x: A table of 17 dungeons, from Ragefire Chasm at levels 13 to 15 up to Scholomance at 57 to 60. Nine new dungeons. Hall of Thanes and Ruins of Lordaeron are already open in the beta.  Joining the Troops The section on group roles includes a table of every dungeon in the game. It has 17 rows. Maraudon and Dire Maul, which veterans think of as part of the original game, aren't on it because they hadn't been built yet. Forever adds nine new dungeons. Two are in the beta: Hall of Thanes for levels 13 to 18 and Ruins of Lordaeron for 15 to 20. The October 1 beta notes add an Excavation Site in the Wetlands. The guide's ideal starter group was a warrior, a mage and a priest, plus two friends. That part has aged fine.

Raids weren't finished, so a designer explains what a raid is and promises Onyxia and Molten Core for launch. The first raids open December 9: Barrow Deeps for 10 players and Hyjal Summit for 20.  Raids The raid chapter is two pages long and contains no strategy at all. Instead there is an interview with Jeffrey Kaplan, then one of the game's designers, who has to start by explaining what a raid even is. He names Onyxia and Molten Core as the launch raids and answers one question with a winking refusal. Forever is set before Molten Core. Its first raids open on December 9, five weeks after launch: Barrow Deeps, for 10 players, and Hyjal Summit, for 20.

A list of twenty things the writers wish someone had told them, including that murlocs are evil. Twenty-two years on, we can't fault a single one.  An Introduction to MMORPGs Near the front of the book is a numbered list of things its writers learned the hard way. The first is that you can't put a space in your character's name. The thirteenth is a three-word warning about murlocs. The last tells you to stop reading and go play. We'll check the mechanical ones, like names, when the live game opens. The murloc one needs no checking.

t: Five tips from 2004 that still work
x: Log out at an inn. Take a gathering profession. Ask questions. Agree the loot rules first. Thank your group. Still the advice we'd give a new player.  An Introduction to MMORPGs The guide's list of do's reads like something a patient friend would tell you. Log out at an inn, because you earn bonus experience while you're away. Pick up a gathering profession early, because mining, skinning and herbalism pay for everything else. Ask questions, then try to find the next answer yourself. Agree who gets what loot before the dungeon, not after. Say "good group" at the end of the night. That last one isn't a game mechanic. It's the reason people still talk about this game twenty years later.

Don't call tauren cows, burgers or big game. Apologise if you get people killed. Say "good group." Having read general chat in the beta, we'd like all three back.  An Introduction to MMORPGs The 2004 guide spends several pages on manners: how to behave while hunting, in town and on a battlefield. Some of it is practical, like not taking a monster someone else is already fighting. Some of it is just kindness written down.

t: The glossary saw the acronyms coming
x: The very first section is a four-page glossary of chat shorthand. Learn a handful and a busy chat channel starts to make sense.  An Introduction to MMORPGs Before it teaches you anything about the game, the guide teaches you to read other players. LFG is looking for group, and LFM is looking for more. WTS and WTB are want to sell and want to buy. PST means send me a private message. DPS is damage per second, a DOT is damage over time, OOM is out of mana, INC is incoming and AFK is away from keyboard. Places get shortened too. SW is Stormwind, IF is Ironforge, UC is Undercity and TB is Thunder Bluff. VC is Van Cleef, the boss of the Deadmines, so "LFG VC" is someone looking for a group for that dungeon.
